name: Text, commentary and gloss (matn, sharḥ, ḥāshiya)
definition: The layers of a madrasa book: the short text learnt by heart (matn), the commentary that explains it (sharḥ), and the gloss written on the commentary (ḥāshiya), sometimes with notes on the gloss (taqrīr).
body: Most books of grammar the madrasas read come in layers. Ibn al-Ḥājib's al-Kāfiya is the matn; Jāmī's al-Fawāʾid al-Ḍiyāʾiyya is a sharḥ on it; ʿAbd al-Ghafūr al-Lārī's and ʿIṣām al-Dīn's are ḥāshiyas on Jāmī. The Alfiyya has the same shape: Ibn ʿAqīl's and al-Ushmūnī's sharḥs, and al-Khuḍarī's and al-Ṣabbān's ḥāshiyas on them.

A sharḥ may be mixed (mamzūj), weaving the matn's words into its own sentences, or set out passage by passage ('his words…, I say…'). A taʿlīq is a looser set of notes. Reading a book with its sharḥ and ḥāshiya is how the madrasa teaches the student to argue.
